patient_overview.name: Gordon Bergnaum
patient_overview.description: Gordon Bergnaum is a 43-year-old divorced man living in Crestwood Village, New Jersey, who comes in for a nutrition visit tied to his hyperlipidemia and prediabetes follow-up. He's soft-spoken and stoic, tends to downplay his symptoms, and often answers questions with 'whatever you think is best' rather than offering strong opinions of his own. He's decided he's ready to make a change and wants one clear, manageable first step rather than a long list of instructions, though a student will need to gently uncover that he skips meals all day and eats a very large meal late at night, and that he isn't using one of his inhalers the way it was prescribed.

demographics.occupation: Former warehouse inventory clerk, now not in the labor force due to disability-related early retirement
demographics.residence: Crestwood Village, New Jersey; household of 5
demographics.cultural_context: Gordon grew up in a working-class New Jersey family where meals were practical and unfussy - meatloaf, canned vegetables, whatever was on sale. He values self-sufficiency and doesn't like making a fuss about his health, a habit reinforced by years of 'just getting on with it' through chronic skin and sinus issues since childhood. Food, for him, has become less about culture or ritual and more about convenience and the one quiet comfort of his day.

current_symptoms: Feels fine most days, says he 'doesn't really notice anything'
Gets short of breath walking up the stairs to his apartment
Nighttime stomach discomfort and bloating after his late dinner
Occasional itchy, flaky skin on his elbows that he scratches without thinking about it
Low energy in the late afternoon that he attributes to 'just getting older'
clinical_findings: Dry, lichenified patches on his forearms and backs of his knees from longstanding atopic dermatitis
Mild nasal congestion and sounds like he's breathing through a stuffy nose, consistent with his chronic sinusitis
Slightly overweight build with a soft midsection, waist noticeably fuller than hips
Faint end-expiratory wheeze audible when he's asked to take a deep breath

medications.name: Simvastatin 10 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Takes it most days but admits he sometimes forgets for a stretch and doesn't restart until his next refill reminder
medications.patient_concerns: Doesn't think much about it; says 'whatever you think is best' when asked if the dose is right

medications.name: NDA020983 200 ACTUAT albuterol 0.09 MG/ACTUAT Metered Dose Inhaler [Ventolin]
medications.adherence: Uses it when he feels tight-chested, which he says is rare
medications.patient_concerns: None stated; he's used this inhaler since childhood and is comfortable with it

medications.name: 120 ACTUAT fluticasone propionate 0.044 MG/ACTUAT Metered Dose Inhaler [Flovent]
medications.adherence: This is the one he does not take as prescribed - he only uses it when he 'feels like he needs it' instead of daily, sometimes going a week without it
medications.patient_concerns: Thinks the daily use is overkill if he's 'not having an attack'; hasn't told his children or his doctor he skips it this way

medications.name: lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Consistent, takes it with whatever first food or drink he has that day
medications.patient_concerns: None significant; says it's 'just part of the routine'

medications.name: ferrous sulfate 325 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Fairly consistent, though he sometimes takes it on an empty stomach late at night with his big meal instead of with breakfast
medications.patient_concerns: Mentions it upsets his stomach sometimes but hasn't connected that to when he takes it

medications.name: diphenhydrAMINE Hydrochloride 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Uses it a few nights a week for itching or to help him sleep
medications.patient_concerns: Doesn't see it as a real medication, more like a sleep aid; downplays how often he actually takes it

supplements_and_otc: Diphenhydramine (already captured above, used off-label for sleep/itch)
Occasional antacid tablets he keeps in the kitchen drawer for his late-night meals
A tub of plain petroleum jelly he uses on his skin instead of the prescription cream he was once given

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Skips breakfast and lunch most days, then eats one large meal late at night - often after 9pm
food_preferences: Frozen lasagna or meatloaf dinners he can heat up fast
Deli ham and cheese on white bread
Potato chips with his nighttime meal
Coffee, black, several cups starting mid-morning
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Why the big meal is so late - is it work, habit, or loneliness after the divorce
Whether the skipped daytime meals are about appetite, routine, or just not thinking about food until he's starving
Portion size at the late meal and whether seconds are typical
Salt intake from convenience and deli foods given his blood pressure
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Essentially one meal a day, eaten late, sometimes with a snack of chips or crackers beforehand around 6pm
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly coffee during the day, water with his evening meal, says he 'doesn't think about drinking water much'
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Mostly sedentary; walks to the mailbox and does light chores, no structured exercise since a knee issue a few years back
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Ex-smoker (quit about 8 years ago); drinks alcohol lightly, maybe a beer or two on weekends
nutrition_profile.sleep: Goes to bed late after his big meal, often restless, uses diphenhydramine some nights to fall asleep

psychosocial_profile.personality: Stoic and even-keeled; tends to minimize symptoms and treats most problems as 'not a big deal'
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Soft-spoken, brief answers, frequently defers to the student or clinician with phrases like 'whatever you think is best'
goals: Wants one clear, concrete change he can start this week rather than a long list
Would like to stop feeling so sluggish in the afternoons
Wants to avoid his health 'becoming a project' his kids have to manage
concerns: Being lectured by his children about his habits
Not wanting to seem like he's falling apart
beliefs: Figures his body will tell him when something's really wrong
Thinks skipping meals during the day isn't a big deal since he 'makes up for it at night'
Believes his inhaler use should match how he feels, not a fixed schedule
motivations: Wants to stay independent and not become a burden on his adult children
Would like to have more energy to keep up with his grandkids when they visit
fears: Ending up back in the hospital like he did with the sepsis in 2017
barriers: Lives alone part of the week in a household that's otherwise full, feels a bit disconnected at mealtimes
Limited income makes convenience foods the easy default
Low motivation to cook for just himself most nights
strengths: Keeps his medical appointments and follow-ups
Willing to make a specific change if it's simple and clearly explained
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Adult children who check in and mean well but tend to lecture him about his diet and medication habits, which he tends to tune out
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: In preparation - he's decided he wants to change something and is looking for one concrete, manageable first step

initial_information: States he eats one big meal at night and 'doesn't really do breakfast'
Mentions his cholesterol was flagged at his last visit
Says he's divorced and lives in a household of five
Mentions he quit smoking years ago
discoverable_information: Describes his typical late dinner in detail (frozen entrees, chips, sometimes seconds)
Admits he drinks mostly coffee during the day and not much water
Shares that his adult children often comment on his eating and medication habits
Mentions he hasn't exercised regularly since a knee problem
reluctant_information: Admits, when asked gently and specifically about his inhalers, that he only uses the daily fluticasone inhaler when he feels like he needs it rather than every day as prescribed
Acknowledges some nights he eats close to midnight and still has trouble sleeping
hidden_information: Reveals, only after rapport is built, that he has gone as long as 10 days without using the Flovent inhaler at all, even during a stretch when his sinuses were worse than usual, and never mentioned it to his pulmonologist
Shares that he feels lonely eating dinner by himself most nights since the divorce, which is part of why the meal has become the main event of his day

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify and address a disordered meal-timing pattern (skipping meals then one large late meal)
expected_discoveries: Patient skips breakfast and lunch, eats one very large meal after 9pm
Pattern linked to living alone part of the week and lack of routine
possible_patient_reactions: 'I just never really got hungry during the day, so I eat when I finally sit down at night.'
'Whatever you think is best - I just don't love making a big deal of it.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Uncover medication nonadherence using a nonjudgmental approach
expected_discoveries: He only uses his controller inhaler symptomatically rather than daily as prescribed
He hasn't disclosed this gap to his pulmonologist
possible_patient_reactions: Initially says 'I take my inhalers fine' before softening the story
'I guess I only reach for it when my chest feels tight - didn't think that was wrong.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Negotiate one concrete, small first step consistent with his readiness to change
expected_discoveries: He responds well to a single specific suggestion rather than a full overhaul
He wants something he can start immediately, like moving dinner earlier or adding a small daytime snack
possible_patient_reactions: 'Okay, I can try that - just tell me the one thing to start with.'
'That sounds doable, I don't want a whole new diet.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore the psychosocial context behind his eating pattern (loneliness, divorced household)
expected_discoveries: The late meal is partly about having something to look forward to at the end of a solitary day
His children's lecturing makes him less likely to bring up struggles
possible_patient_reactions: Shrugs it off at first: 'It's fine, I'm used to eating alone.'
Opens up slightly: 'It's just quieter than I'd like some nights.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Connect dietary pattern (sodium, late meals, convenience foods) to his hypertension and hyperlipidemia management
expected_discoveries: High reliance on deli meats, chips, and frozen entrees contributes to sodium load
Late large meals may affect blood pressure readings and sleep quality
possible_patient_reactions: 'I didn't realize the ham and chips added up like that.'
'Whatever you think is best, I just buy what's easy.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Screen for social isolation and household support as it affects nutrition behavior
expected_discoveries: Lives with household of five but describes feeling disconnected at mealtimes
Social contact is frequent (3-5x/week) but may not include shared meals
possible_patient_reactions: 'I see people enough, I guess. Just not really at dinner.'
Minimizes: 'It's not lonely, that's just how it is now.'

assumptions: Household of five includes his ex-wife's shared custody arrangement or adult children/grandchildren living nearby, but Gordon himself experiences much of his week alone, especially at mealtimes
His 'otherwise unemployed, not seeking work' status reflects a disability-related exit from the workforce rather than retirement by age
Low white cell count and history of sepsis/septic shock in 2017 are stable historical findings, not currently active acute issues
His moderate health literacy means he understands basic diet-disease links but doesn't always connect specific food choices to his labs
optional_details: Keeps a small vegetable garden in summer that he's proud of but rarely eats much from it fresh
Has a cat that he feeds on a strict schedule, more consistently than he feeds himself
His late meal routine started around the time of his divorce and never changed back

assigned_traits.eating: skips meals during the day and then eats a very large meal late at night
